\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{हादसा} (hādsā)}{हादसा (hādsā)}]{\hi{हादसा} (hādsā) — a mishap; an accident}

\label{lesson:HI-C298-hadsa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to be grazed, then the Hindi for covered in blood.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{हादसा}}
\textbf{\hi{हादसा}} — \emph{hādsā} — \textquotedblleft{}a mishap; an accident\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{हादसे} \hi{की} \hi{वजह} \hi{यह} \hi{थी} \hi{कि} \hi{ड्राइवर} \hi{बहुत} \hi{तेज़} \hi{गाड़ी} \hi{चला} \hi{रहा} \hi{था।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hādse kī vajah yah thī ki ḍrāivar bahut tez gāṛī calā rahā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cause of the accident was that the driver was going too fast.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{हादसा}} (\emph{hādsā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥāditha}, \textquotedblleft{}something that happens\textquotedblright{}. It is the everyday word beside the formal \textbf{\hi{दुर्घटना}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hādsā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hādsā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hādse kī vajah yah thī ki ḍrāivar bahut tez gāṛī calā rahā thā.} — The cause of the accident was that the driver was going too fast.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to be grazed, then the Hindi for covered in blood, then say \emph{hādsā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{हादसा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A mishap; an accident\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{घायल} (ghāyal)}{घायल (ghāyal)}]{\hi{घायल} (ghāyal) — injured; wounded}

\label{lesson:HI-C298-ghayal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for covered in blood, then the Hindi for a mishap.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{घायल}}
\textbf{\hi{घायल}} — \emph{ghāyal} — \textquotedblleft{}injured; wounded\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{हादसे} \hi{में} \hi{दस} \hi{लोग} \hi{घायल} \hi{हुए।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hādse meṁ das log ghāyal hue.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Ten people were injured in the accident.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{घायल}} (\emph{ghāyal}) is built on \emph{ghāy}, a wound, which CDIAL 4460 lists for Hindi under Sanskrit \emph{ghāta}, \textquotedblleft{}a blow\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\hi{घायल} \hi{होना}} is to be injured: \textbf{\hi{दस} \hi{लोग} \hi{घायल} \hi{हुए}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghāyal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghāyal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hādse meṁ das log ghāyal hue.} — Ten people were injured in the accident.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for covered in blood, then the Hindi for a mishap, then say \emph{ghāyal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{घायल} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Injured; wounded\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{बेहोश} (behoś)}{बेहोश (behoś)}]{\hi{बेहोश} (behoś) — unconscious}

\label{lesson:HI-C298-behos}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a mishap, then the Hindi for injured.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{बेहोश}}
\textbf{\hi{बेहोश}} — \emph{behoś} — \textquotedblleft{}unconscious\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{ड्राइवर} \hi{बेहोश} \hi{था।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍrāivar behoś thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The driver was unconscious.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{बेहोश}} (\emph{behoś}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bē}, \textquotedblleft{}without\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{hōš}, \textquotedblleft{}the senses\textquotedblright{}, the same \emph{hōš} that sits inside \textbf{\hi{होशियार}}, alert.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{behoś}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{behoś}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍrāivar behoś thā.} — The driver was unconscious.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a mishap, then the Hindi for injured, then say \emph{behoś} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{कुचलना} (kucalnā)}{कुचलना (kucalnā)}]{\hi{कुचलना} (kucalnā) — to crush; to run over}

\label{lesson:HI-C298-kucalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for injured, then the Hindi for unconscious.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{कुचलना}}
\textbf{\hi{कुचलना}} — \emph{kucalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to crush; to run over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{एक} \hi{ट्रक} \hi{ने} \hi{उसकी} \hi{साइकिल} \hi{कुचल} \hi{दी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ek ṭrak ne uskī sāikil kucal dī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A lorry ran over his bicycle.
\end{quote}

Past, with \hi{ने} (he or she …): \hi{उसने} \hi{साँप} \hi{को} \hi{कुचला}, \emph{usne sā̃p ko kuclā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{कुचलना}} (\emph{kucalnā}) is listed by CDIAL under \emph{*kucyatē}, \textquotedblleft{}is contracted, is bent\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3221), with Hindi \emph{kucalnā}, to trample on. A wheel or a foot that \textbf{\hi{कुचलता} \hi{है}} leaves the thing flattened.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kucalnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kucalnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ek ṭrak ne uskī sāikil kucal dī.} — A lorry ran over his bicycle.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for injured, then the Hindi for unconscious, then say \emph{kucalnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{सँभलना} (sãbhalnā)}{सँभलना (sãbhalnā)}]{\hi{सँभलना} (sãbhalnā) — to steady oneself; to recover}

\label{lesson:HI-C298-sambhalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for unconscious, then the Hindi for to crush.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सँभलना}}
\textbf{\hi{सँभलना}} — \emph{sãbhalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to steady oneself; to recover\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{थोड़ी} \hi{देर} \hi{बाद} \hi{वह} \hi{सँभला} \hi{और} \hi{उठा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{thoṛī der bād vah sãbhlā aur uṭhā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After a little while he steadied himself and got up.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \hi{वह} \hi{सँभल} \hi{गया}, \emph{vah sãbhal gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{सँभलना}} (\emph{sãbhalnā}) is the intransitive partner of \textbf{\hi{सँभालना}}, to look after, and CDIAL 12961 lists both under Sanskrit \emph{saṁbharati}, \textquotedblleft{}brings together\textquotedblright{}. You \textbf{\hi{सँभलते} \hi{हैं}} when you pull yourself together after a fall or a shock.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sãbhalnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sãbhalnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thoṛī der bād vah sãbhlā aur uṭhā.} — After a little while he steadied himself and got up.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for unconscious, then the Hindi for to crush, then say \emph{sãbhalnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
